implementation_notes: In C the algorithm is written literally with C11 atomic_compare_exchange_weak on a _Atomic pointer, and the two auxiliary schemes are hand-rolled: hazard pointers need a per-thread hazard record array that every reader publishes its pointer into before dereferencing, and epochs need per-thread epoch counters plus a global epoch that advances only when every thread has moved past the current one. C has no memory safety net, so the reclamation protocol is a raw-pointer discipline with no compiler help - which is why production C uses published pseudocode verbatim rather than adapting it. The practical alternative in C is single-linked lists with a Michael-Scott queue and never freeing removed nodes (the type-preserving allocator), trading memory for correctness.
idiom_name: C11 atomic CAS loops with a hand-rolled hazard-pointer or epoch reclamation layer
pitfalls: The seq_cst fence between publishing the hazard and re-reading the pointer is what makes the hazard-pointer protocol safe; omit it and the node can be freed between the store and the re-check.
A hazard slot per simultaneous outstanding read is required - two nested reads on one slot silently corrupt the protocol.
Freeing a node while any thread's hazard record names it is a use-after-free; the scan must be exact, not approximate.
C gives no ownership tracking, so a double-free or a stale pointer is silent corruption; the published pseudocode should be used as-is.
